precepts.text: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it. That is it right there. So the congregation is Israel. Is it the church, the Baptist church, the Catholic church? No.
precepts.point: Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit. God said, regardless of all the technological power you have got, you are going to be brought down to hell. America, Babylon, Lucifer.
precepts.why:
To prove who the congregation is, one more: “All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.”

That is it right there. The congregation is Israel. Not the church, not the Baptist church, not the Catholic church: the congregation of Israel, the ones commanded to keep the passover.

So read Isaiah again: “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation”: that is Israel. “in the sides of the north”: that is North America. “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: that is airplanes and helicopters. “I will be like the most High”: I will be like God. “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.” Regardless of all the technological power they have, America, Babylon, Lucifer is going to be brought down to hell.

And he is the one “that opened not the house of his prisoners”. We are the prisoners, the congregation he sat on, but our people believe they are free.

precepts.text: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Leviticus 23 lays out the feasts of the Lord, seven of them in that chapter, and every single one of them represents Jesus Christ. The first annual one is the Lord’s passover, “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even”, the high holy day we just celebrated. So we go back to the instructions for the passover lamb.

“Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats”. Without blemish, a male of the first year. That is the lamb our forefathers had to choose.

That lamb without blemish is the pattern of Christ. The passover is a representation of Christ laying down his life for us, and everything spoken of the lamb in Exodus 12 points to him.

precepts.text: Neither shall ye break a bone thereof: the instruction for slaughtering the passover lamb.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Still in the passover instructions: “In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.”

Neither shall ye break a bone thereof. Those are the instructions for how to slaughter the lamb: do not break the bones of it.

That one command is going to be fulfilled to the letter in Christ. The high holy day of passover that we just went over is a picture of him, down to his bones.

precepts.text: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? You will pull this out on a brother in the street about his tattoos, and meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy: if you are out there with the leaven in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if you both do not repent.
precepts.point: Whosoever eateth leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off from Israel: how do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps in your mind and you say, I do not like that brother; you are spiritually consuming it. That is how you get cut off from your people. This is a serious thing.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses”. That is purging the old leaven. We had to do it physically, but it is something spiritual today. So what is your house today? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” You, me, we are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God is to dwell in us because our temple was destroyed.

Look at how we purge leaven from the house. Brothers dump out the toaster, sweep underneath the floor mats and in the corners where stuff builds up. There is not one grain of yeast in the house. Meanwhile the brother has an evil eye toward another brother, or is bitter toward his wife, or vice versa. We sweep our houses with diligence; we must do the same with our spirit, because we are the temple of God.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” You will pull this out on a brother in the street: brother, you got tattoos, you got the devil on you, you are defiling your temple. We know tattoos are wrong. But meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If you are out there with the leaven of bitterness in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if he and you do not repent.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord, who is our Passover, who set the example. That is the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins.
precepts.point: Whosoever eateth leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off from Israel: how do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps in your mind and you say, I do not like that brother; you are spiritually consuming it. That is how you get cut off from your people. This is a serious thing.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” What is that really saying? How do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps into your mind and you say, damn, I don't like that brother. You are spiritually consuming it, entertaining sin and not purging the leaven from your house. That is how you get cut off from your people, and this is a serious thing.

How you get cut off: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Christ is our Passover, who set the example. That is the gift, the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins, because we are in a wicked place.

And Exodus 13:7 says “there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” We do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, Passover or not. Don't be the brother who does not throw the bread out but puts it in his storage closet and brings it back when Passover is over: laying the bitterness aside for the season and picking right back up hating the brother. That is not the spirit. Throw it out. Let it go.

precepts.text: Ye are not your own; ye are bought with a price, with Christ's blood. When we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He bought us back; when a brother lends you something, you take extra care of it. So glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.
precepts.point: Whosoever eateth leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off from Israel: how do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps in your mind and you say, I do not like that brother; you are spiritually consuming it. That is how you get cut off from your people. This is a serious thing.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Some brothers say, I am going to tuck mine in, tuck away my hatred and my bitterness and save it for later. Paul answers that: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?”

We are not our own. So when we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, whatever sins we deal with, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He is our Passover, our sacrifice; he bought us back, twice he bought us back. So we do not own our bodies to even have the angle to defile our temple. When a brother lends you something, you are supposed to take extra care of it. Christ gave us our bodies and bought us back again, and we need to keep them like brand new.

“For ye are bought with a price”: with Christ's blood. Then, “therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” We have to use our bodies to glorify him in every way possible, and our spirit too, because both belong to God. When we hold back malice, hatred for our brothers or hatred for our wife, we put that on Christ, and it is not of the Lord. We have to let go of that spirit.

That is the leaven Exodus 12:15 says to put out of your house: not only the yeast on the box, but the bitterness tucked in when Bishop comes around and let out again when he leaves.

precepts.text: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.
precepts.point: And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time: time is singular, times is plural, and the dividing is the half; that is three and a half, as Revelation explains.
precepts.why:
The “he” of Daniel 7:25 is the fourth kingdom Daniel did not understand, which the angel revealed to Ezra as the eagle with three heads: Rome, America and Britain. Daniel says “he shall speak great words against the most High”, blasphemies, “and shall wear out the saints of the most High”. Like a pair of sneakers worn so long you cannot tell what brand they were, slavery wore us out until nobody recognizes us as the Israelites, the glorious and mighty sons and daughters of God. People go, those are some damn black Africans. Now you look at a negro Latino and you go, I don't know what the hell that is. That thing, a negro, was made up, and nobody can identify them people as a race.

Then the part about time: he shall “think to change times and laws”. To see what he changed, go to what God set. “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.”

God himself appointed the first month of the year for Israel, at the time he brought them out of Egypt. The new year is not a date man picks. It is an ordinance of God, and it is one of the times the fourth beast thought to change.

precepts.text: Remember this day in which ye came out from Egypt.
precepts.point: January is not the new year.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
In Egypt the Lord told Moses and Aaron, “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you”. Jump to verse 11 to see what holiday comes in that month: “ye shall eat it in haste: it is the Lord’s passover”. So Passover comes in the first month. But what is the name of that first month?

Exodus 13 tells us: “And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten. This day came ye out in the month Abib”.

Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear. It marks the start of the year, the time of Passover and the firstfruits, renewal and freedom from Egypt. So the first month, the month of Passover, is the spring month. Not January.

That matters, because the months of the year are all from Rome. January is named for Janus, the Roman god of beginnings, and America, exercising all the power of the first beast, has the whole earth keeping Rome's new year. The Most High set the beginning of months in the spring, the month we came out of the house of bondage.

precepts.text: Observe the month of Abib and keep the passover.
precepts.point: January is not the new year.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 16:1 is where Moses names the month again with the Passover. It joins the Passover and the month of Abib together, the same as Exodus 13, which says of the night we came out of Egypt, “This day came ye out in the month Abib”. The first month of Exodus 12:2, “the beginning of months”, is Abib, the spring month when the tender barley ears appear.

So the biblical new year does not begin in January. It begins in the spring, at Abib, and each month begins with the moon. January is from the Roman god Janus, who presided over doorways, time and new years.

Who changed it? Daniel 7:25 says the beast “shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws”. The great words are the lies Rome spoke against the Most High: a white man who died for the sins of everybody on the planet, that you must be dumped in the water to be saved, Lent, Christmas and December 25th. Wearing out the saints is the slavery. And changing times and laws is moving the beginning of the year from spring to January, and even daylight saving time. Keeping Abib is coming back to the Most High's times.

precepts.text: The sojourning of the children of Israel in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and it ended the selfsame day; the prophecy was fulfilled at the Exodus.
precepts.point: Abram himself would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age; and the seed would return in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full.

note.label: Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years

precepts.why:
“The sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.” The four hundred years spoken to Abram was an approximation of that time. “At the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt.”

That is the fulfilment of Genesis 15:13. The strange land was Egypt, the affliction was Egypt’s bondage, and it ended at the Exodus, the selfsame day the four hundred and thirty years were up.

So this verse is not the doctrine about America and 1619. The prophecy of the four hundred years was fulfilled when Israel came out of Egypt.

precepts.text: Egypt urged them out in haste, and the Lord gave the people favour, and they spoiled the Egyptians; they came out with great substance.
precepts.point: Abram himself would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age; and the seed would return in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full.

note.label: Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years

precepts.why:
“Afterward shall they come out with great substance.” Here is how it happened. “The Egyptians were urgent upon the people, that they might send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We be all dead men.” The children of Israel did according to the word of Moses, “and they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment.”

“The Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.” The nation they served was judged, and they walked out of it with the silver, gold and raiment of Egypt, just as the Lord had told Abram: great substance.

precepts.text: The children of Israel borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment; and the LORD gave the people favour, so that they lent unto them such things as they required: and they spoiled the Egyptians.
precepts.point: It happened exactly the way it was spoken: after the firstborn of Egypt were slain, the Egyptians lent Israel what they required, and they spoiled the Egyptians.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
At the bush the Lord promised: “I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty”. Every woman would borrow of her neighbour jewels of silver, jewels of gold and raiment, “and ye shall spoil the Egyptians.”

It happened exactly the way it was spoken. After the firstborn of Egypt were slain, “the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment: And the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.”

precepts.text: This day came ye out in the month Abib; the exodus month is the first month of the year.
precepts.point: Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter; that is another lie taught in Babylon.
precepts.why:
“This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” Which month is it? Moses names it: “This day came ye out in the month Abib.” The month Israel came out of Egypt is Abib, and Abib is the first month of the year.

Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter. That is another lie taught in Babylon. The year the Most High gave Israel begins with the month he brought them out.

precepts.text: The meat, drink, holydays, and sabbaths are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ; the Passover lamb was a precursor of him.
precepts.point: The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel.
precepts.why:
“Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats”. The lamb is a foreshadowing. “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

The feast days and the sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, and the body that casts the shadow is Christ. The Passover lamb taken on the tenth day, a lamb for an house, was a precursor of him. So the ordinance in Egypt is not only about a lamb; it is pointing forward to the one the lamb stands for.

precepts.text: The precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, foreordained before the foundation of the world.
precepts.point: The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel.
precepts.why:
The lamb had to be “without blemish, a male of the first year”. Peter shows who that lamb is: “the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot: Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you”.

The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless. He was verily foreordained before the foundation of the world, before ever a lamb was taken in Egypt, but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel. The Passover lamb, a shadow of things to come, is the shadow of him.

precepts.text: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us; therefore let us keep the feast, with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
precepts.point: This day is a memorial, a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, kept by an ordinance for ever. It was not done away; even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, therefore let us keep the feast. The lamb of the Passover represents Christ, and the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away.
precepts.why:
“ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.” For ever means it was not done away. Even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.”

The lamb of the Passover represents Christ; Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. And the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away. “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” The memorial the Lord gave in Egypt, throughout your generations by an ordinance for ever, is the feast Paul tells us to keep, with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

precepts.text: The spirit of life from God entered into them and they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon them which saw them.
precepts.point: The feast of unleavened bread is observed because in this selfsame day the Most High brought the armies of Israel out of Egypt. He deals with armies, and when he brings Israel out of this place he is bringing out an army again: when the spirit of life enters them and they stand upon their feet, great fear falls on them which see them, for they stand up an exceeding great army, not choir boys.
precepts.why:
“in this selfsame day have I brought your armies out of the land of Egypt”. The Most High deals with armies. Israel did not come out of Egypt as a crowd; they came out as armies, and when he brings Israel out of this place he is bringing out an army again.

John saw it: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” When the spirit of life enters them and they stand upon their feet, great fear falls on them which see them. They are not choir boys; that is why the fear falls. They are the same armies the Lord brought out of Egypt on this selfsame day, standing up again.

precepts.text: The breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army; that is why they fear.
precepts.point: The feast of unleavened bread is observed because in this selfsame day the Most High brought the armies of Israel out of Egypt. He deals with armies, and when he brings Israel out of this place he is bringing out an army again: when the spirit of life enters them and they stand upon their feet, great fear falls on them which see them, for they stand up an exceeding great army, not choir boys.
precepts.why:
Ezekiel shows what stands up when the spirit of life enters Israel: “So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” Not choir boys, an exceeding great army. That is why great fear falls on them which see them.

The Lord brought “your armies out of the land of Egypt” in this selfsame day, and the feast of unleavened bread is kept for it by an ordinance for ever. He deals with armies. When he brings Israel out of this place, the breath comes into them, they stand up upon their feet, and it is an army again.

precepts.text: He that hateth his brother is in darkness and knoweth not whither he goeth, because darkness hath blinded his eyes.
precepts.point: For seven days no leaven is found in the houses; whoever eats that which is leavened, whether stranger or born in the land, is cut off from the congregation of Israel.
precepts.why:
“In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.” The Passover begins at even and ends at even because the day begins and ends at even. It is not difficult; the scripture says it plainly.

Yet many fell away from the truth over this very point of the day beginning at evening. Sin puts blinders on. “But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.” When you hate your brother you are in darkness, and darkness blinds the eyes; you cannot see what the scripture plainly says, even something as simple as at even.

So the ones who could not see when the Passover begins were not lacking a verse. They were in darkness, and did not know whither they went.

precepts.text: The almighty word leaped down from heaven as a fierce man of war; the destroyer in Egypt was the word of God.
precepts.point: The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.
precepts.why:
“the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.” Who was the destroyer? The Wisdom of Solomon tells it.

“For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction, And brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war, and standing up filled all things with death. The destroyer was the word of God.

And the destruction was total. “there sounded an ill according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was carried abroad for children that were bewailed. The master and the servant were punished after one manner; and like as the king, so suffered the common person. So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them”. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury.

“For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” The enchantments had kept them from believing; the death of the firstborn made them acknowledge Israel to be the sons of God. That is why none of Israel was to go out at the door until the morning: the word of God was in the land of destruction that night, and the Lord passed over the door where he saw the blood and would not suffer the destroyer to come in.

precepts.text: The Word was with God, and the Word was God; Christ is the almighty word that slew the firstborn in Egypt.
precepts.point: The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.
precepts.why:
The destroyer that filled Egypt with death was the almighty word of God, and John says who the Word is: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word was with God, and the Word was God. That is Christ.

So the destroyer was Christ. The almighty word that leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war, that stood up and filled all things with death, is the same Word that was in the beginning with God. Christ slew the firstborn in Egypt, and where the Lord saw the blood on the lintel and the two side posts he passed over the door and would not suffer the destroyer to come in.

precepts.text: He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death, not to the idols of Egypt.
precepts.point: In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. Unto God the Lord belong the issues from death; the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death.
precepts.why:
“at midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.” Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died. From the throne to the dungeon, nothing in Egypt stood between the Lord and any firstborn.

In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. “He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death.” The issues from death belong to the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not to the idols of Egypt. He is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death; that midnight in Egypt, life and death were in his hand and no one else's.

precepts.text: Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; Pharaoh's threat against Moses could not stand.
precepts.point: The Egyptians were urgent upon the people to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, We be all dead men.
precepts.why:
The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again. Now he “called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, and get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve the Lord, as ye have said. Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also.”

“Saying, Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm.” Pharaoh's threat against Moses could not stand, because Moses was the Lord's anointed and his prophet. The man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone: from a threat of death to “bless me also.” There was not a house in Egypt where there was not one dead, and the Egyptians were urgent to send Israel out, saying, “We be all dead men.” The Lord's prophet was not touched; Egypt was.

precepts.text: They departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the morrow after the passover.
precepts.point: The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children. Israel departed from Rameses in the first month; the exodus is tied to Rameses by name.
precepts.why:
“And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children.” The exodus is tied to Rameses by name, and Numbers dates it: “they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.”

Israel departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day, the morrow after the passover, with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians. Six hundred thousand men on foot beside children, leaving Rameses openly the morrow after the passover: the same departure, the same place, the same month.

precepts.text: The bondmen are of the heathen and the strangers, a possession for ever; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour.
precepts.point: The law sets the order: bondmen and bondmaids are to be of the heathen round about and of the strangers that sojourn among you; they are a possession and an inheritance for the children. But over the brethren, the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.
precepts.why:
“And a mixed multitude went up also with them”. The mixed multitude that left Egypt with Israel were not to be among the children of Israel as rulers. The law sets the order of who is who.

“Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids. Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession. And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever”. The bondmen and bondmaids are of the heathen round about and of the strangers that sojourn among Israel; they are a possession and an inheritance for the children, for ever.

“but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.” The brethren are not ruled with rigour by one another, and the strangers that went up with Israel are not the rulers. That is the order for the mixed multitude that came out of Egypt.

precepts.text: These things were done that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken; Christ is the Passover lamb.
precepts.point: Thus did all the children of Israel as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, and the selfsame day the Lord brought them out of the land of Egypt by their armies.
precepts.why:
“In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.” Not a bone of the Passover lamb was to be broken. That also goes to Christ, the Passover lamb.

On the cross his bones were not broken, and John says why: “For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.” The scripture being fulfilled is this ordinance of the passover. What was commanded of the lamb in Egypt was kept in the body of Christ, because he is the lamb the ordinance was about.

precepts.text: Your lamb shall be without blemish; it was taken out from the sheep, kept from the goats to the fourteenth day, and roasted with fire, not raw nor sodden.
precepts.point: The Passover lamb shows how that was carried out. The lamb was without blemish, a male of the first year, taken out from the sheep and kept from the goats, because if it got in a fight it would take a blemish, a bruise, a cut. It was kept up to the fourteenth day, isolated and given nothing but water, so that it purified itself; and it was eaten roast with fire, not raw and not sodden with water, with the purtenance thereof, for after those days there was nothing left within it.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
The Passover lamb shows how offering without blemish was carried out. “Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats”. It was taken out from the sheep and kept from the goats, because if it got in a fight it would take a blemish, a bruise, a cut.

Then “ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month”: from the tenth day to the fourteenth it was isolated and given nothing but water, so that it purified itself. Then the whole assembly killed it in the evening, struck the blood on the two side posts and the upper door post, and ate the flesh that night “roast with fire, and unleavened bread; and with bitter herbs”.

“Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast with fire; his head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof.” It was eaten with the purtenance, for after those days there was nothing left within it.

Whatever the sacrifice is for the Lord, it has to be the best of the best, a flawless sacrifice, no bruise, no cut, no stain, nothing superfluous. The lamb that had no blemish was symbolic of Christ.

precepts.text: A mixed multitude of other nations went up with Israel out of Egypt.
precepts.point: They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.
precepts.why:
“And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting.” Who were they? “And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.” The mixed multitude were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel, who went up with the people out of Egypt.

It was not Israel complaining at first; it was the nations lusting after the food of Egypt, and “the children of Israel also wept again.” Gullible and assimilated as always, Israel followed right after them and murmured against their God.

The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it.

precepts.text: The Most High commanded that this month be the beginning of months, and that on the fourteenth day the whole congregation kill the lamb without blemish in the evening.
precepts.point: He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
precepts.why:
The Lord spake to Moses and Aaron in Egypt: “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” Every man was to take a lamb “according to the house of their fathers”, “without blemish, a male of the first year”, and keep it “until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening.”

Josiah kept it exactly. “Josiah kept a passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem: and they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.” He kept the laws pertaining to the Passover, in the month the Most High made the beginning of months.

He set it in order: he “set the priests in their charges, and encouraged them to the service of the house of the Lord”, told the Levites to “Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel did build”, and to “prepare yourselves by the houses of your fathers, after your courses”, so the whole congregation could do “according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.”

precepts.text: This day is to be a memorial kept as a feast to the Lord throughout all generations, an ordinance for ever.
precepts.point: He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
precepts.why:
“And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the Lord throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.”

The Passover is a memorial kept as a feast to the Lord throughout all generations, an ordinance for ever. That is why Josiah kept it, and why he charged the Levites, “serve now the Lord your God, and his people Israel”, and to “kill the passover”, “that they may do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.”

precepts.text: No stranger was to eat the passover, so the feast was never meant for other nations.
precepts.point: The feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10 commemorates the Maccabees driving out the Greeks and rededicating the temple the Greeks had profaned. Christ would not turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto Moses and Aaron, This is the ordinance of the passover: There shall no stranger eat thereof”.

No stranger was to eat the passover, so the feast was never meant for other nations. The Greeks who came up to worship at the feast in John 12 could not have been heathen; they were Israelites keeping the ordinance.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 18: Babylon Is Fallen

precepts.why: “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” The year begins in the month of Abib, in the spring; your friendly neighborhood white man says January 1st, in the winter. So he changed that time.

note.label: The Truth Behind Christmas and New Years

points: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months, the first month of the year. The month is Abib, the month in which Israel came out of Egypt.

Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter; that is another lie taught in Babylon.

In the tenth day of the month every man was to take a lamb according to the house of his fathers; if the household was too little for the lamb, he and his neighbour next unto his house were to take it according to the number of the souls.

The lamb was to be without blemish, a male of the first year, taken from the sheep or from the goats. This is a foreshadowing: the feast days and sacrifices are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ.
The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel.
The whole assembly of the congregation of Israel was to kill the lamb in the evening, and take of the blood and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses.

The flesh was to be eaten that night, roast with fire, with unleavened bread and with bitter herbs. That is the Passover menu in layman's terms: lamb roast with fire, unleavened bread, bitter herbs; no fried chicken, no birthday cake, no mashed potatoes and gravy, none of the thirteen herbs and spices.

Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water: do not boil it, but roast it with fire, the head with the legs and the purtenance thereof, and let nothing of it remain until the morning; what remains is burned with fire.
It was to be eaten with loins girded, shoes on the feet, and staff in hand, in haste: it is the Lord's passover, and that very night Israel was leaving Egypt.

The Lord would pass through the land that night and smite all the firstborn of man and beast, and against all the gods of Egypt he would execute judgment. Each plague put an Egyptian god to shame: when he smote the land with darkness he showed that the sun god Ra is no god at all, for the God of heaven and earth blotted out the sun three days. Israel had to learn that those gods are nothing, because the nation was about to come out and serve the one true God.

The blood was a token upon the houses: when I see the blood, I will pass over you. That is where the term Passover comes from; the houses with the blood on the doorposts were passed over from death while the firstborn of Egypt were slain.

This day is a memorial, a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, kept by an ordinance for ever. It was not done away; even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, therefore let us keep the feast. The lamb of the Passover represents Christ, and the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away.

Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day the leaven is put out of the houses, and whosoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
The first day and the seventh day are holy convocations; no manner of work is done in them save that which every man must eat, meaning the food may be cooked.

The feast of unleavened bread is observed because in this selfsame day the Most High brought the armies of Israel out of Egypt. He deals with armies, and when he brings Israel out of this place he is bringing out an army again: when the spirit of life enters them and they stand upon their feet, great fear falls on them which see them, for they stand up an exceeding great army, not choir boys.

In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even. The Passover begins and ends at even because the day begins and ends at even; it is not difficult.
For seven days no leaven is found in the houses; whoever eats that which is leavened, whether stranger or born in the land, is cut off from the congregation of Israel.

The elders were to draw out a lamb for their families and kill the passover, take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts; the hyssop bush was used like a paintbrush to paint the blood of the lamb over the doorposts.

None of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning: stay inside, for the Lord passes through to smite the Egyptians, and where he sees the blood he will pass over the door and will not suffer the destroyer to come in to smite you.

The destroyer was Christ, the almighty word of God. In the quiet silence of that night the almighty word leaped down from heaven out of the royal throne as a fierce man of war into the midst of the land of destruction, and standing up filled all things with death. The Egyptians cried for the children that were bewailed; master and servant, king and common person suffered after one manner, and the dead were too many to bury. Upon the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.

This thing is an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever, kept even when Israel comes into the land the Lord promised. When the children ask, What mean ye by this service? the answer is, It is the sacrifice of the Lord's passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when he smote the Egyptians and delivered our houses.

The feast days commemorate the Most High delivering his people and bringing judgment on their enemies; that is the same pattern the feast of dedication commemorates. The people bowed the head and worshipped, and the children of Israel went and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

At midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle. Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died.

In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. Unto God the Lord belong the issues from death; the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death.
Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again; now he called for Moses and Aaron by night, saying, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, go, serve the Lord as ye have said, take your flocks and your herds, and bless me also. Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; the man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone.
The Egyptians were urgent upon the people to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, We be all dead men.
The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.

As Moses had said, they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment; the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent them what they required, and they spoiled the Egyptians. They took everything.

The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children. Israel departed from Rameses in the first month; the exodus is tied to Rameses by name.
A mixed multitude went up also with them, and flocks and herds, even very much cattle. The mixed multitude that left with Israel were not to be among the children of Israel as rulers.

The law sets the order: bondmen and bondmaids are to be of the heathen round about and of the strangers that sojourn among you; they are a possession and an inheritance for the children. But over the brethren, the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.
They baked unleavened cakes of the dough brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt and could not tarry, neither had they prepared any victual.

The sojourning of the children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day, all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt.
It is a night to be much observed unto the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is the Passover night, which all the children of Israel are to observe in their generations.
It is eaten in one house, none of the flesh carried outside, neither shall ye break a bone thereof. That also goes to Christ, the Passover lamb, whose bones were not broken on the cross.

This is the ordinance of the passover: no stranger eats of it. A bought servant may eat when he is circumcised; a foreigner and an hired servant shall not eat thereof. When a stranger will keep the passover of the Lord, let all his males be circumcised, and he shall be as one born in the land; one law is to the homeborn and to the stranger.
Thus did all the children of Israel as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, and the selfsame day the Lord brought them out of the land of Egypt by their armies.
